steps: A receives lease token 41 and writes to storage.
A pauses long enough for its lease to expire.
B acquires ownership with higher token 42.
Storage accepts 42 and rejects delayed operations carrying stale token 41.

lesson.scenario: A storage writer rejects work from a paused lease holder after ownership moves to a newer token.

steps.title: First ownership
steps.narration: The lock service grants A token 91.
steps.outcome: A can write only by presenting token 91.
steps.invariant: Each ownership grant must carry a token greater than every prior grant.

steps.title: A pauses
steps.narration: A stops renewing but retains stale in-memory authority.
steps.outcome: The lock is available while A is unaware.
steps.invariant: Process pauses can outlive a lease and invalidate local ownership beliefs.

steps.title: B gets newer token
steps.narration: The lock service grants B token 92.
steps.outcome: B has a newer ownership generation.
steps.invariant: Token order, not arrival time at the client, defines freshness.

steps.title: Resource advances fence
steps.narration: The volume accepts B’s write and records max token 92.
steps.outcome: The protected resource advances its durable fence.
steps.invariant: The resource must atomically compare the token with the side effect.

steps.title: Stale holder rejected
steps.narration: A resumes, but its token 91 is lower than the stored fence.
steps.outcome: A cannot overwrite B despite resuming late.
steps.invariant: Every side-effecting path must enforce the fencing token.

production.scenario: A subscription-renewal platform lets only the current shard owner charge customers by attaching fencing tokens to every billing write, even when a crashed worker comes back late.
components: Starts the 02:00 customer-renewal workload for shard 12
Issues monotonically increasing shard tokens for each renewal shard
Processes shard 12 while token 9081 is current
Takes over shard 12 after the east worker misses heartbeats
Turns renewal jobs into capture requests for the card processor
Authoritative charge-attempt history keyed by shard token
Captures late retries that arrive with an obsolete token
flows: assign shard 12 for the 02:00 renewal run
The planner asks for a fresh ownership generation before any worker starts charging customers in that shard.
Worker east becomes the only valid owner and must include token 9081 on every state change.
The active worker sends card captures through the payment adapter while its token is still current.
The billing ledger records the attempt only because token 9081 is the highest generation it has seen for shard 12.
grant token 9082 after east lease timeout
After a heartbeat gap, the ownership service hands the shard to worker west with a newer token.
If the old worker wakes up and retries, the ledger rejects the write because token 9081 is now fenced off by token 9082.
Operations can inspect the rejected retry and confirm that the stale worker never mutated billing state after failover.
